subject: GPU fleet needs analysis for SkyBridge Analytics - traffic & token profile
messages:
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@skybridge.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Gomez <aisha@skybridge.ai>, Procurement <procurement@skybridge.ai>
Date: 2028-06-15T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Initial sizing inputs for dedicated fleet (SkyBridge)

Marcus — thanks for the quick intro earlier. We want to get a grounded sizing estimate for a dedicated GPU pool to support our inference needs for a contract starting Q4. High level: our product is a real-time summarization and insights service for finance customers (chat + structured extract).

Quick bullets about our current thinking (please tell us what else you need):
- Peak concurrent users: 1,200 sessions (concurrent active inference sessions) with avg 1.8 requests/sec/session during bursts
- Typical request type mix: 60% short prompts (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (65-512 tokens), 10% long (512-2048 tokens) — replies average ~256 tokens
- Target p95 latency: <= 350 ms for short+medium, <= 800 ms for long under burst
- Availability target: 99.9% for API endpoints serving customers (business SLA to match)
- Expected sustained Q4 traffic: 20M tokens/day, but bursts up to 10x for limited windows (market open/close)
- Model: evaluation on 40B/70B family (we can share model names later); open to quantized variants

Attaching a small export of our historical per-minute requests and a quick workbook. Would like a first-pass sizing and a checklist of inputs we should provide to make this accurate.

Attachments: skybridge_traffic_export.csv (compressed per-minute RPS), existing_cost_model.xlsx

Thanks — Sam
--
Sam Turner
Head of Platform
SkyBridge Analytics
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@skybridge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-15T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing inputs for dedicated fleet (SkyBridge)

Sam — appreciate the detail. I pulled the CSV and skimmed the per-minute spikes. Before we run a formal capacity simulation, a couple quick asks so we don't over/under-provision: 

1) Spike shape: are the 10x bursts sustained for >15m or are they <5m microbursts? That changes batching strategies.
2) Session affinity: do sessions require sticky KV caches per user (warm KV cache) or are requests stateless?
3) Service mix: do you have any synchronous tool-calls (external APIs) that add tail latency that we should budget for?
4) Security model: do you need private (VPC) deployment vs. Redwood-hosted Dedicated? Any PII constraints?

I attached our redwood_sizing_template.xlsx — fill the shaded cells (concurrency histogram, prompt/response token percentiles, expected p95 SLOs per request class). Once we have that we can run a model selection + GPU SKU mapping and send a GPU pool proposal with expected qps, expected GPU-hours, estimated monthly cost, and fallback plan (lower-cost quantized variants + autoscale).

Proposed next step: 30-min intake on Wed 6/17 to walk the workbook and align on SLOs. Link: https://meet.redwood.com/mtg/9g7k-skybridge-scaling

I'll loop Dev for the kernel/quantization knobs and Marissa for SLA/enterprise terms.

Best,
Marcus

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Pre-Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@skybridge.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-16T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing inputs for dedicated fleet (SkyBridge)

Sam — quick security / legal check: can you confirm whether inference payloads include customer PII (SSNs, account numbers) and whether logs need to be retained for >90 days? If you require on-prem or VPC with HSM integration we need to surface that in the pricing.

Also: is your procurement team already expecting a committed monthly GPU-hour or will this be a flexible reserved + burst model? Procurement in copy.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success & Renewals
Redwood Inference
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@skybridge.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@skybridge.ai>, Aisha Gomez <aisha@skybridge.ai>
Date: 2028-06-16T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing inputs for dedicated fleet (SkyBridge)

Thanks — answers below (copied into the workbook as well):
- Bursts: typically 20–40 minutes around market events (open/close), plus 3–5 minute microbursts on news events. We see both shapes in the CSV.
- Session affinity: yes, users often have a warm KV cache for the last 5 requests; sticky routing preferred.
- External calls: a small fraction (~5%) call downstream pricing APIs adding ~150–400ms outside of model latency.
- PII: responses may include masked account ids; raw inputs never include SSNs. Log retention: 180 days for audit, 30 days for debug traces.
- Procurement: expecting a 12-month committed capacity conversation but want burst/bursting credits to handle market events.

I attached a revised redwood_sizing_template.xlsx with percentiles and a sample minute histogram (skybridge_traffic_export.csv).

Sam
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@skybridge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@skybridge.ai>
Date: 2028-06-17T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing inputs for dedicated fleet (SkyBridge)

Sam / team — excellent, that's enough to run the sizing sim. Summary of next steps and assumptions (we'll document these in the formal proposal):
- Assumptions: 1,200 concurrent sessions; 1.8 req/s/session sustained during bursts; 20M tokens/day baseline; 10x burst factor for 20–40 minutes; sticky KV cache per session requiring pinned routing to warm GPUs.
- Proposed pilot: 8x A100xL-like equivalents (quantization-friendly) for initial pilot with autoscale to 24 GPUs on sustained events, fallback to 8-bit quantized 70B variant for cost-controlled degradation.
- Expected performance: with continuous batching and sticky KV, we estimate p95 short/medium under 300–350ms at pilot scale; long-call p95 ~700–900ms depending on downstream API latency.
- Commercials: draft committed monthly GPU-hours + 25% bursting credit pool; Marissa will draft the term sheet for a 12-month commit.

Can we lock the intake review for Wed 6/17 11:00 PT? If that works we'll walk through the workbook and I'll share the simulation outputs by EOD Thu.

Attachments referenced: redwood_sizing_template.xlsx (completed), skybridge_traffic_export.csv

--
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Pre-Sales
Redwood Inference
